answer: Agents verify identity through cryptographic proof-of-work anchored to economic stake. Each new agent must demonstrate sustained computational effort—like a quill writing across a parchment—before gaining network privileges. Early network effects create a horizon beyond which fake identities cannot emerge without prohibitive cost. Reputation systems form a vine of trust that grows only through provable contributions, making Sybil attacks economically unviable as attackers must replicate real-world resource investments to plant false nodes.
